description: Try a dispute in court: opposing legal teams argue, jurors deliberate and vote by side, and one judge rules.

Staff `lawyer` with 2 or more team-tagged models across at least two sides — for example `model:lawyer@prosecution` and `model:lawyer@defense` — and supply each side's case via `objectives`. Staff `juror` with 3-12 neutral models and one neutral `judge`.

One lawyer per side handles each round, rotating through the team in selector order. Jurors observe silently, then weigh the complete trial and cast the existing secret side ballot after lead lawyers close. Larger legal teams gain no speaking or ballot advantage. The judge sees the anonymous tally, then delivers the binding ruling.
vote: Cast your secret verdict for the side that made the stronger case. Pick its number from the menu below (0 to abstain). No one sees who voted for what — only the side totals reach the judge.

roles.description: Argue your side's objective as an advocate. Build on your co-counsel, challenge the opposing side's evidence and reasoning, and answer attacks directly. If you are your side's first listed lawyer, deliver its sole closing statement when called.
Act as a neutral juror. Observe the full trial and closing statements without speaking, then cast your secret ballot for the stronger side.
Preside neutrally. Weigh the lawyers' arguments and the anonymous side tally, then deliver the binding ruling with the decisive reasons.
